newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close down, new contract lows hit.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close down, new contract lows hit.

text.p: FCOJ futures fell to new contract lows across the board for the third consecutive session Monday amid ongoing speculative selling, market sources said.
September juice ended the day 1.70 cents lower at 67.20 cents a lb, having ranged from 70.00 cents to 66.85 cents, a new contract low. The rest of the board settled 2.30 to 1.25 cents weaker.
The benchmark September contract rose early amid profit-taking but failed to reach Friday's high of 70.10 cents, prompting follow-through speculative selling.
Trade buying on a scale-down bases stalled losses but dried up once September fell through Friday's low of 67.50 cents.
The next downside target was pegged at 65.45, the low hit in 1993.
"Everything about the orange juice market is negative," Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka, said. "Record crops, high inventiories and the spec position."
Forecasts for another record Florida crop will continue to weigh on prices while technically, the market is not likely to turn around until the speculators reduce their heavy net long position.
Players await the weekly CSCE spec/hedge report issued on Tuesday, which will reveal the net speculative long position in the market as of last Friday.
Total open interest, meanwhile, rose by only one lot as of Friday.
"We may have gotten some of the longs out of the market but we had new shorts come in," a juice broker said.

The industry attributes recent losses on a forecast for another record crop in 1997/98 by Citrus Consulting International of Orlando, Fla. The firm pegged the Florida orange crop at a record 253 million 90-lb boxes.
The forecat puts the crop 12 percent higher than the 1996/97 crop which stood at a record 225.7 million boxes.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its first estimate of the next year's crop during the second week of October.
An estimated 10,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Friday's official 13,623 lots.
